comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Stages three and four of MIP-2, which is now Accepted and carries the whole design. The first two landed on `main3` (slot 3 of the 2026-09-02 parallel round); these did not, and this says what is left and why they were not started rather than half-started.

## What is left

**A window holds an ordered list of Muster tabs, one on screen.** Regions become the parts of that tab rather than one column per machine, `cmd+1` and `cmd+2` switch between a local tab and a devenv tab, and the sidebar flattens to tabs with their panes under them. This is the change `a_2HtF52Itm` asked for by name.

**A Muster tab holds member tabs on several machines**, so one tab can hold a laptop pane beside a devenv pane. This is the only part that turns a daemon guarantee into a Muster one: a tab spanning two machines can only live in Muster's file, and the durability answer is to degrade per tab - every tab that exists today is single-machine and keeps the guarantee it has.

## Why they were not started

**They land together or not at all.** A window shows every machine at once today, side by side. Stage three on its own replaces that with one tab filling the window, and grouping - stage four - is what puts the two side by side again. Landing three alone would take away an arrangement people are using and give back nothing until four arrived.

Together they are a change to the composition record, the roster's wire shape, the sidebar, the numbered chords, the saved format and the durability table. That is more than could be finished and made green in the round this was raised in, and a half-landed model change is worse than none - especially with three branches to fold together.

## What is already in place for it

- `Region` and the saved arrangement no longer carry a workspace, so the record this change rewrites is one noun smaller (MIP-2 stage one).
- Each window has its own arrangement file, so "which tabs is this window showing" is a per-window question with a per-window answer (stage two).
- `View::showing()` is derived from "a region shows a tab, and a tab on screen has its panes on screen unless a zoom covers them", which is stated in terms this change does not move, and pinned in all 51 composition cases.
- The durability answer is confirmed and written into MIP-2 rather than left as the thing the Draft was waiting on.

## What it answers when it lands

`a_2I6h18OU6` - closing a machine's last pane stops refilling it, because `open_remaining_regions` stops existing in its present form and nothing is owed a column.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Moved to the top of `next` on 2026-09-02. This is the card that ends the two-process workaround, and the workaround's bill came due today.

The setup it replaces: the devenv window runs from `~/.muster` with the local daemon commented out, and a second Muster is launched as a separate instance with `--home ~/.muster-local` for a local-only window. That exists because a window is a column per machine and an emptied machine refills (`a_2I6h18OU6`). What it costs, all found in one day of use:

- Two processes are two applications to macOS, so AltTab's per-app switching shows one window or the other, never both (`a_2I6h18OU6`, comment of 2026-09-02).
- Two configs to keep in step, two arrangements to migrate, two relaunch procedures - the local one needs `open -n -a Muster --args --home ...` and a person who remembers it.
- Every fix to a `[[daemon]]` block is applied twice or missed once. The `ControlPersist` workaround (`a_2J1KZ9FbM`) went into one config today.

## The full model is the priority, not a slice of it

An earlier version of this comment floated landing stage three alone, on the grounds that the one person using the side-by-side arrangement had already stopped. Retracted: the ask is to solve this properly, so both stages ship together as MIP-2 sequences them. Stage three replaces "every machine on screen at once" with one tab filling the window; stage four is what gives the side-by-side back and is the stage that turns a daemon durability guarantee into a Muster one. Splitting them to reach one process a few days sooner is the kind of shortcut that leaves a half-migrated model, which MIP-2 already argues is worse than none.

## Why the chain to it is short

Everything this depends on has landed. Stage one (the core stops naming a workspace) and stage two (each window keeps its own arrangement) are in. The shakedown fixes MIP-2 says it has to survive are done, and the second-window and pane-move bugs the umbrella card lists are fixed or measured. So the proper path to one process is not a stack of prerequisite tickets - it is this card, done in full, with its five open questions settled first.

## Settle these before writing code (MIP-2 Open Questions)

- Where a machine's own states go once there is no per-machine heading - the `connected` / `disconnected` / `holding nothing` states, and the empty-machine case `a_2HpkpfIfq` was about. MIP-2 says this probably has to be solved first or together.
- Where the machine label goes on a row, and how it stays quiet when only one machine is attached.
- What `muster window --json` says once `regions[]` stops being machine-shaped.
- What happens to an existing `window.toml` - read each saved region as a single-machine tab, or open fresh.

## Related but not on this path

`a_2IZ6Of6JP` (two windows showing one pane) is not required for the window-per-monitor layout: two windows showing different machines show different terminals, so the one-client-per-terminal limit never bites. It only matters for handing the same pane between windows, which is a separate want.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Plan for stages three and four, written before starting, from the 2026-09-03 parallel round (slot 1, branch `main1`). Alexander is away for this round, so everything the MIP left open is settled below rather than asked about. ## The model, concretely **A Muster tab is a `TabId` with a member on each machine that has panes in it.** The registry in `names.rs` already mints `t1w3r07bsd` on first sight of a backend tab; the change is that one name may now be bound to a member on more than one daemon. `Registry` gains that cardinality for tabs and keeps it at one for panes, because a pane is a process and lives where it lives. Two things follow, and they are why this shape was picked over the alternatives. The mirror does not move. A mirror is per daemon, so within one a `TabId` still resolves to exactly one backend tab: `mirror.tab()`, `mirror.panes_in_tab()` and `Pane.tab` all keep their meaning, and `reconcile` stays per daemon with no cross-daemon ordering invented. And the grouping lands in `~/.muster/state/names.toml`, which is where it has to be for the arrangement file to name only Muster's own ids - a `[[tab]]` row already carries `name`, `daemon` and `backend`, so a grouped tab is two rows sharing a name and the format does not change. **A window holds an ordered list of those tabs and shows one:** struct Composition { daemons, tabs: Vec, showing: Option, next_region } struct MusterTab { id: TabId, regions: Vec, focused: Option } struct Region { id, daemon, weight, pane } // `tab` moves up to the owner `Composition::regions()` answers with the showing tab's regions, so `View::of`, `Roster::of` and the shell's `RegionStrip` keep the shape they have. A region is still a column. What changed is that the columns divide a tab rather than the window, and there is one per machine holding panes in that tab rather than one per machine attached. Switching tabs is already cheap on the Swift side: `PaneSurfaces` keys surfaces by pane and parks them when no region shows one (`a_2HzbwzO32`), so a tab switch costs no bridge and, on a devenv, none of the 440ms an ssh session takes. ## The four open questions **Where the machine goes on a row.** On the pane row, at its trailing edge. A tab row says nothing about machines: a tab may span two, so any single answer it gave would be wrong for some of its panes. **How it stays quiet.** It is not drawn at all while one daemon is attached, which is the common case and leaves that window exactly as it reads today. Labelling only the machines that are not this one was the alternative and costs more than it saves: with two devenvs attached, a reader has to already know that a blank means local. **Where a machine's own states go.** A machines section at the foot of the sidebar, holding a row per daemon that is disconnected or holding no panes. A daemon that is connected and holding panes contributes no row - its panes carry its name. Picking a row there asks for a pane on that machine, which is the affordance `a_2HpkpfIfq` deferred and what makes deleting `open_remaining_regions` safe rather than a reopening of the hole that card closed. The roster carries the machines so the sidebar can draw them; `muster window` keeps its fuller `Machine` answer, which says host, socket and who started the daemon. **What `muster window --json` says.** `regions[]` keeps its name and becomes the parts of the tab on screen - `region`, `daemon`, `pane`, `weight`, `keyboard`, `zoomed` - and drops `tab`, because every region in it now shows the same tab. A new top-level `showing` names that tab. `tabs[]` drops `daemon` and gains `daemons`, the machines it holds panes on. `panes[]` does not change; it already says both `daemon` and `tab`. **And a fifth the MIP raised in passing.** It says the sidebar's on-screen mark should be removed with the change. Half of that: the mark that meant "these tabs share the screen" is gone, because nothing shares the screen any more. What replaces it is the ordinary current-tab mark every tab strip has, on the one tab the window is showing. `RosterTab.on_screen` keeps its name and means that. ## Migration, which is decided An existing version 3 arrangement - one region per machine - becomes **one Muster tab holding all of it**, so the first launch after this lands looks like the last launch before it. Where the saved regions name two machines' tabs, the second is bound as a member of the first under the first's name, and the launch logs that it did. Every other tab a daemon holds becomes a Muster tab of one, appended in the order the daemon lists them. The file goes to version 4. `[[region]]` gains `tab` and swaps the top-level `focused` index for a `keyboard = true` on at most one region per tab - an index into a list that is filtered on read is the fragile half of that record, and per-tab focus is what makes switching away and back land where you left. ## What gets deleted `open_remaining_regions` goes. Nothing is owed a column, so closing a machine's last pane leaves it empty (`a_2I6h18OU6`), and `muster pane new --daemon ` and the new sidebar row are the two ways back. `open_a_workspace_if_the_window_is_empty` stays as it is: it is about a window with nothing in it, which is still a state worth filling. The rule that a window somebody asked for opens onto tabs of its own stays too - it now decides which tab is *showing* rather than which regions exist. ## Grouping, which is stage four The gesture is `muster pane move --pane

--tab `: if `t` has no member on `p`'s machine, one is made there, bound under `t`'s name, and `p` moves into it. `MoveDestination` gains a third arm for it. `pane move --onto ` stays refused across machines, because that asks for two panes in one tree and a tree is one daemon's. Dragging a pane row onto a tab caption in the sidebar sends the same request, which is the gesture for somebody who never opens a terminal. ## How it lands Roughly one commit each, green at each step where that is possible: 1. `Registry` lets a tab name have a member per daemon. Nothing else changes; no tab has two yet. 2. `Composition` holds the ordered tab list and shows one. `Region` loses `tab`. `open_remaining_regions` goes. Saved format 4, with the version 3 migration. 3. The roster flattens to tabs with panes under them, and carries the machines. Proto, CLI and sidebar follow. 4. Grouping: the new `MoveDestination` arm, the herdr adapter making a member tab, the CLI flag, the sidebar drop. 5. Docs: `architecture.md` durability in two tiers, `glossary.md` stops calling a tab daemon truth, `docs/cli/`, and this MIP's History and Open Questions. ## What I expect to hurt The conformance corpus. `composition.json` is 51 cases and `roster.json` 38, and both are authored prose as much as data. Fourteen composition cases put `local` and `devenv` on a tab both daemons call `w1:t1`; under `Mint::Backend` those two become one Muster tab, which is the new cross-machine case rather than the two separate tabs they were written as. Those get devenv ids of their own, and a handful of new cases pin grouping deliberately. The numbered chords are the part most likely to break quietly. Both spellings keep working and `panes` stays the default; `a_2A6T9c2r4` is not mine to decide and nothing here decides it. `a_2Hx68fXqr` - one tab in the window numbers panes - gets more honest rather than less, because a window holding one tab now means one tab rather than one per machine.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Built on `main1` (slot 1 of the 2026-09-03 parallel round), stages three and four together. Four commits: the registry, stage three, stage four, the docs. The gate is green, and so are `./dev --contract` and `./dev --ssh`. ## The shape it took **A Muster tab is a `TabId` with a member on each machine holding panes in it.** The registry already minted `t1w3r07bsd` on first sight of a backend tab; one name can now be bound to a member on more than one daemon. That kept the mirror where it was - a mirror is per daemon, so within one a `TabId` still resolves to exactly one backend tab - and it put the grouping in `~/.muster/state/names.toml`, which is the only place it can live: neither daemon knows the other exists, so neither can be asked which of its tabs is half of something. **A window holds an ordered list of them and shows one.** Regions moved onto the tab: one per machine with panes in it, which is one for every tab until somebody groups two. `Region` lost its `tab` field, because the tab now owns the list it is in. Switching tabs costs nothing on the Swift side. `PaneSurfaces` already keyed surfaces by pane and parked them (`a_2HzbwzO32`), so a tab switch spawns no bridge and, on a devenv, pays none of the 440ms an ssh session takes. ## The open questions, answered Written into MIP-2 in place, and into the docs beside them. - **Where the machine goes:** on the pane row, at its trailing edge. A tab row says nothing about machines - a tab may span two, so any single answer there would be wrong for some of its panes. - **How it stays quiet:** it is not drawn at all while one machine is attached, which is the common case and leaves that window reading exactly as it did. Labelling only the machines that are not this one loses more than it saves - with two devenvs attached, a reader has to already know that a blank means local. - **Where a machine's own states go:** a machines section at the foot of the agent list, holding a row per machine that is unreachable or holding no panes. A machine that is connected and holding panes contributes no row; its panes carry its name. Picking a row there asks for a pane on that machine, which is the affordance `a_2HpkpfIfq` deferred - and what makes deleting the refill rule safe. - **What `muster window --json` says:** `regions[]` keeps its name and becomes the parts of the tab on screen, dropping `tab` because they all show the same one; a top-level `showing` names it; `tabs[]` trades `daemon` for `daemons`. The MIP also said the sidebar's on-screen mark should be removed. Half of it was: the mark that meant "these tabs share the screen" is gone, because nothing shares the screen. What replaced it is the ordinary current-tab mark every tab strip has - a flat list of tabs with nothing saying which one you are looking at would be worse than the mismatch the mark was added to fix. ## Migration A version 3 arrangement becomes one Muster tab holding all of it, so the first launch after this lands looks like the last launch before it. The file goes to version 4 and version 3 is read rather than refused. `[[region]]` rows now name their tab and carry `keyboard = true` on the one that had it, and the file names the tab it was showing. The grouping a migration implies cannot be done by the file reader - it is a change to the name registry - so `Saved` carries it out and the seam applies it before any daemon has spoken. Doing it later would leave the mirror holding names decoded before the rebinding. ## What `a_2I6h18OU6` asked for Done. `open_remaining_regions` is gone, nothing is owed a column, and a machine you have finished with stays empty. The two ways back are `muster pane new --daemon ` and the machine's own row in the agent list. ## Three things I loosened or tightened that the MIP did not ask about Each is in the MIP's History with its reasoning. - **Closing needed a region showing the thing; it now needs only that the window holds it.** Every tab but one is in the background once a window shows one at a time, so the old rule would have made `muster tab close --tab` and `muster pane close --pane` refuse nearly every name a script could give them. What the rule protected against - acting on a session this window is not attached to - is still refused, and the agent list names every tab and every pane, so you can still see what you are about to destroy. **This is the one I would most like a second opinion on**: it is a real safety loosening, and the alternative is a `tab close` that can only close the tab you are looking at. - **`--daemon` with no pane falls back further**, to that machine's first pane anywhere in the window. It was the keyboard's pane on that machine, then that machine's region; a machine whose tabs are all in the background has neither, which is now ordinary. - **A window asks a machine for a workspace only once that machine has spoken.** Asking in the moment before a first snapshot lands opened a tab nobody wanted and left the one they did behind. This was also what made `bridge_death` flaky. ## Stage four, as a gesture `muster pane move --pane

--tab `, and dragging a row onto a tab caption in the agent list. The pane stays on its machine; what moves is which Muster tab it belongs to. `MoveDestination` gained a third arm for it, and `--onto` still refuses across machines - that orders two panes against each other and both have to be in one tree. The adapter has two shapes and neither needs a daemon to know anything new. A tab this machine already holds part of takes the pane into that part; a tab it holds no part of gets one, and the answer's tab is bound as that Muster tab's member here. ## What the numbered chords did Nothing. Both spellings still work, `panes` is still the default, and `a_2Hx68fXqr` - one tab in the window numbers panes - is more honest than it was, because that now means one tab rather than one per machine. `a_2A6T9c2r4` stays in `in-progress`. ## The corpus `composition.json`, `roster.json` and `composition-saved.json` were rewritten. Fourteen composition cases had put `local` and `devenv` on a tab both daemons call `w1:t1`; under `Mint::Backend` those two are now one Muster tab, so they became the cross-machine case and the ones that meant two separate tabs got devenv ids of their own. Six new composition cases and one new roster case pin the new model's own rules, and four in `tab-names.json` pin grouping. One thing the corpus cannot express: the branch where a machine holds no part of a tab. Under `Mint::Backend` every name resolves, so `crates/muster-seam/tests/across_machines.rs` pins it against two real daemons instead - which is the honest place, since only the window can see a tab holding panes on two machines.

creator: Alexander Terp
title: 🧩 A Muster tab that spans machines, and one on screen at a time
